nodes.statement: The constraints define a finite-dimensional linear subspace of the target function space. The network width must span this subspace. Since the subspace dimension is intrinsic to the constraint equations and independent of the number of sampling points $w$, the minimum width $N_c$ remains constant.

The constraints sample a manifold whose intrinsic dimension scales with $w$ (e.g., each new constraint activates a new dimension in the input space or feature space). Approximating functions on a higher-dimensional manifold requires exponentially or linearly more neurons (curse of dimensionality).

The constraints are subject to effective stochasticity (numerical or sampling noise). To achieve zero violation on hold-out points with high confidence, the network must over-parameterize to control generalization error. Sample complexity theory suggests width scales with the square root of the number of constraints to maintain error bounds.
